newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian airlines back down on local fare hike.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian airlines back down on local fare hike.

text.p: Nigerian airlines on Monday flinched from their resolve to increase domestic air fares by 200 percent after a warning against the move by the aviation ministry, airline officials said.
"We are charging the normal fare," said an official of the Aviation Development Company, the leading domestic flyer.
The 200 percent increase in local air fares announced by the Nigerian Airline Operators (AON) last Thursday was to go into effect on Monday.
But the aviation ministry described it as illegal, saying any airline that effected it would be grounded.
"I paid the same fare as I have always paid when I flew to Lagos this afternoon from (the capital) Abuja," said one passenger.

AON had argued that jacking up the fares was the only way to keep the airline industry healthy. If it went into effect, a one-way economy ticket to the capital Abuja from Lagos, a distance of about 800 km (500 miles) would cost 7,920 naira ($99), three times the current price of 2,685 naira ($34).
The airlines have long campaigned for an increase in domestic airfares, saying this would help sustain their operations in an economy that has been in recession for years.
In November, the military government cancelled what it called an "insensitive" 100 percent increase in domestic air fares annnounced by AON.
